entities.summary: Sigismund Albicus was a Czech medical doctor, lawyer, and Roman Catholic Archbishop of Prague. He played a crucial role in the development of the University of Prague, which became a hub for scholarly pursuits during the 14th century. Albicus' contributions to the field of medicine, particularly in the area of anatomy, were instrumental in shaping the understanding of human physiology. His work on the subject was widely influential, inspiring future generations of medical professionals. The establishment of the Archiepiscopal Medical Court, which he founded, marked a significant milestone in the integration of medicine and law. This innovative approach to medical governance set a precedent for future reforms in the field. As Archbishop of Prague, Albicus worked tirelessly to promote education, particularly among the clergy, and his efforts helped to raise the status of the university. He also played a key role in the development of the Prague Corpus Christi, a grand procession that showcased the city's devotion to the Eucharist. In 1427, Albicus passed away, leaving behind a legacy of academic excellence and medical innovation that would continue to inspire future scholars. His impact on the cultural and intellectual landscape of 14th-century Prague remains a testament to his enduring influence.
